transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?
My moods have been all over the place lately, and I feel wound up and irritated with everyone at home. It just feels like I'm constantly on edge and snapping at my family.
When your mood changes, how long do these different states usually last—do they shift from hour to hour within the same day, or do they last for several days at a time?

This revved-up, buzzing energy and lack of sleep has actually been going on constantly, every single day for about a month now. My immediate emotions can swing in a second from feeling on top of the world to snapping in hot anger, but that overall wound-up feeling lasts all day. It doesn't really switch back to normal.
Have you ever experienced periods in the past where you felt the opposite—extremely down, sad, or exhausted, lasting for weeks at a time?

No, I haven't really experienced periods of feeling extremely down or exhausted like that in the past. It's really been the opposite lately—I just feel so wound up, irritable, and constantly on the go.
Is this the very first time in your life you've experienced a period of high energy and decreased need for sleep lasting for weeks, or have you had similar episodes in the past?
I don't recall ever having an episode quite like this in the past, so I'm really not sure. This past month has just been incredibly intense and unlike anything I've ever experienced before.

Even if it wasn't as intense as this past month, have you ever had shorter periods in your life—lasting just a few days—where you felt unusually happy, highly productive, or needed much less sleep than usual?
No, I haven't really noticed or experienced shorter periods like that in the past. This past month is the first time I've ever felt this level of intense energy, irritability, and constant activity.
How has this intense energy and irritability affected your daily life, such as your work, relationships, or ability to manage your responsibilities?

It has caused a lot of trouble; at my warehouse job, I've been making mistakes and leaving tasks half-finished. At home, my constant arguing, overspending on supplies, and overcommitting have strained my family relationships so much that my husband and pastor insisted I get help because they feel I'm spinning out of control.
During this past month, have you experienced anything unusual, like hearing voices, seeing things others can't, or feeling like you have special powers?
No, I haven't experienced anything like that at all. I haven't heard any voices, seen things that aren't there, or felt like I have any special powers.
Are you currently taking any new medications, or have you been using any substances like recreational drugs, alcohol, or high amounts of caffeine lately?
No, I haven't started any new medications, and I don't use recreational drugs or alcohol. I only drink my normal amount of coffee in the morning, nothing extra.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a one-month history of a sustained irritable and elevated mood, accompanied by increased energy, a decreased need for sleep, distractibility (leaving tasks unfinished at work), and reckless behavior (overspending and overcommitting). This has caused significant functional impairment in both her job and her family relationships. She has no prior history of depressive, manic, or hypomanic episodes, and there are no psychotic symptoms or substance-use factors present. This clinical picture meets the ICD-10 criteria for a manic episode without psychotic symptoms (F30.1). Hypomania (F30.0) is ruled out due to the severity of the functional impairment and the duration of the symptoms.
